record_notes.DCP-LETT-1977: Sunday assigned October 19, 1856 after London visit, four blocks and both notes read. Seeds safely received; abrupt departure from Hooker dinner to catch train does not prove earlier offered dinner dates. Gray botanical-geography opinion relayed orally. Hawk pellets and partridge-foot mud arrived, not all seeds germinated. Experimental-book event sequence in apparatus distinguishes October 14 preparation, October 16 pellet, October 19 planting. No preserved current incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1983: November 9, 1856 Hooker ALS plus separate memorandum, all thirty blocks, exclusions, full notes/annotations/bibliography and both actual diagrams read. P1 manuscript reading complete, praise qualified by stiff first half and pencil corrections; tentative greater openness to change, not wholesale conversion. P2–5 tropical cooling, icebergs, east–west migration and northern-island objections. P6 thanks missing Darwin note received November 9 and offers November 12/14 dinners. Owen attack reported hearsay, manuscript return at Club prospective, P10 Lyell question. P11–30 memorandum is separately transmitted, probably later, known by November 15, not automatically November 9 or November 11. Notes A/I through H followed by further propositions address glacial migration, isotherms, gentians, representative species, tropical survival and humidity. Figures show schematic Europe/America isotherms and unlabelled inclined section. Undated Darwin annotations and response quoted in footnote 20 are separate voices. Main letter supports 1986; precise oral objection in 1989 is absent, so do not pair its whole theory response to this memorandum.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1986: November 11 main letter, explicitly Wednesday November 12 postscript, year supplied. Eleven blocks, notes and bibliography read. Main P1 thanks Hooker manuscript verdict, P2 conditionally accepts dinner and proposes discussion. P3–5 new experiments: five seedlings from four kinds survived eagle pellets, damp pellet delay a confound; bird-dung seeds and partridge mud distinct. Later November 13 nothing came up note concerns partridge-earth experiment, not all eagle seeds. P6 Raoul paper just read, possible land/intervening islands qualified. P7 harbour-mud Salter report read sceptically; footnote names James Salter, bibliography lists John William’s unrelated starfish article, a source-reference mismatch. P10–11 cancels dinner due Emma preference, proposes work-only visit; 5½ o’clock is genuine MathML, not 512. Main and later reply sections must retain separate dates.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1989: November 15, supplied 1856, five blocks and all notes. All Hooker manuscript notes now available, but comprehensive consideration deferred for weeks. Particular warm-temperate versus sub-arctic objection was apparently made orally and is absent from preserved 1983 letter/memorandum. Darwin explains longer exposure to foreign associates under modification, acknowledges serious difficulty and asks no answer. P4 morning mammal-distribution blow identified in apparatus as Daniell November 14: later full-source knowledge lead, not accepted here. Do not invent the oral question or make general subject overlap a direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1622: Sunday assigned November 16, 1856, five blocks and complete annotations/notes/bibliography. Hooker explicitly answers 1989 with distance, time and greater modifying exposure objection to the sub-arctic migration account. Numbered points survive in body. Separate two-page Darwin note develops his answer and contains revisions/deletions; undated private working prose is not incoming Hooker or automatically November 16 public response. Directly answered in 1991 P2. Low catalogue number is not earlier chronology.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1991: November 18 with year supplied, five blocks and all notes. P1 forwards Gray-to-Hooker enclosure received that morning plus Gray-to-Darwin letter, identifies northern-range facts and friendly conifer paradox criticism. Whole bundle transmission gives Gray knowledge by November 18; exact arrival phrase directly attaches to Hooker enclosure, so do not overstate separate Darwin-letter receipt. P2 explicitly thanks Hooker note received this morning and answers 1622 twice-distance objection with migration en masse versus changed associates. Thus exact November 18 receipt for 1622 is supported. P3 genuine MathML twenty-one and one-half hours in owl, not 2112; 400–500-mile transport is hypothetical storm distance, not observed flight. Mid-Atlantic sightings separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1995: November 22, 1856 incomplete Hooker letter, six surviving blocks, all notes and Darwin annotations. Gray letter to Hooker concerns debt for Thomson purchases, not botanical content; possible later botanical letter promised. P2–3 answer Darwin migration explanation, ask efficient causes, challenge time/conditions/associates distinction and suggest latent characters. P4 recommends owl-seed notice, not proof Darwin published it. P5 Gray paradox/conifer discussion breaks off at Like. P6 raspberry seed identification originally above salutation, not a reconstructed ending. Darwin marginal disagreement and Candolle-credit comment undated; latter cannot restore missing Hooker prose. Directly answered in 1997 P2–3 and reversely answers 1991.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1997: November 23 with year supplied, five blocks and full apparatus. P1 asks no answer. P2 explicitly answers Hooker convertible terms challenge: external conditions may cause variability but selection chiefly forms marked varieties/species, with time important as opportunity for selection and associates more important than external conditions; author stresses uncertainty. P3 directly answers publication suggestion and raspberry identification, nine dung-seed kinds now found. P4 Candolle justice remark responds material missing from surviving Hooker ending; do not manufacture it from Darwin annotation. Retain direct response P2–3 rather than whole body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1966: Hooker early December 1856 letter, seven blocks, all notes/bibliography. Singleton month envelope in XML is December 1–31; display early December remains qualified. Tulasne report, personally gathered Khasia plants, absence from Himalaya, permanently wet beds and Kerguelen Limosella air bubble distinguish observation from inference. Preserved spirit bottle examination is future, occasional stream drying/crossing admitted possible. This is an ANSWER to 1974 request and supplementary revision, not the antecedent to Darwin original question. No exact receipt date; finished chapter date alone cannot create one.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1974: Early December 1856 Darwin ALS with later Hooker corrections, six blocks and full notes/bibliography. Requests return with remarks, gives provisional Podostemon passage incorrectly placing observation in Himalaya, tests underwater pollen possibility from Lindley and asks illumination. Original Darwin wording differs from full revised passage printed in footnote 5: Hooker corrects to Khasia/Eastern Bengal, annual habit and exceptions to underwater flowering. Corrected prose and deleted interrogation marks are different hands/layers, not Darwin already knowing the answer. 1966 follows this inquiry, likely accompanying returned manuscript; date and returned extent uncertain. It remains an outgoing query/grounding record, not accepted Darwin reply to 1966.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2008: December 1 with year supplied, four blocks, all notes/bibliography. Requests Hooker mark 700–800-species NZ list for trees and separated sexes if remembered without laborious consultation; tree/bush boundary arbitrary, England comparison uses Loudon. List copied by amanuensis exists elsewhere but full list is not transcribed. Asks whether to send manuscript, so delivery not yet established; separate germinated bird-dung seed enclosed for genus identification. Later lost seed is apparatus, not already known December 1. 2014 answers this precise list task.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2014: December 7, 1856 Hooker ALS, fifteen retained blocks, all notes/annotations/bibliography. Rough NZ counts and uncertain mono/dioecious categories deliberately qualified. Body says 756 species, 108 trees, 150 shrubs; table rows total 757 and 149 shrubs, as Darwin separately totals. Do not silently reconcile. Table: herbs 379/102/19, shrubs 88/30/31, trees 56/40/12; 102 includes 55 Compositae. 234 separated/incomplete flowers matches column combination, taxonomic and developmental caveats remain. Raw diag/ramme and flattened rows require rendering care. Tasmania review promised in months. P11 private Lyell review-authorship anecdote and P13 Emma inquiry separately answered in 2018. P14–15 additional Clematis/Viola/Compositae/grass qualifications, separate undated Darwin calculations not Hooker original conclusions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2018: December 10 with year supplied, eight blocks and full apparatus. P1 thanks tree counts, finds trees in 38 families and separated sexes in half, regards association likely while explanatory hypothesis remains uncertain. Tasmania report future; growing chapter length unrelated. P2 answers wife inquiry plus separate Mrs Hooker note. P3 answers Lyell anecdote but Darwin has not seen the review. P4 torpid molluscs after seven days immersion show as yet one revival among sinkers and one among floaters, not universal survival; egg experiment failed. P6 Francis suggested floating carcass, pigeon 30-day trial succeeded for seeds including tares; 999/1000 predation is hypothetical objection, not measured probability. P7 oral freshwater difficulty and P8 Harvey approach new requests. Direct scope P1 tree portion, P2 first sentence and P3, not experiments.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2022: December 24 with year supplied, six blocks and all notes/bibliography. Missing Hooker reference on Leguminosae, uncertainty on Campanulaceae and unknown Portlock letter remain missing. Proposed Harvey inquiry not yet sent/answered. Species-definition comparison distinguishes naturalists emphasis and invokes previously read Aquilegia example; no single preserved incoming source supports whole discussion. Supposes black seed lost, rather than verified custody outcome. About a dozen dung seeds now, distinct from November nine kinds. No forced pair to 2014 because general botanical subjects overlap.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2040: January 17, supplied 1857, two blocks and complete notes/bibliography. Friday January 16 Daniell/Bennett discussions after January 15 Club. Advice on possible grant and collector project, not award or expedition already executed. Daniell zeal/experience, Hooker reservations, Bennett qualified support and perceived mortality risk are attributed reports. Darwin will follow consultation; no preserved specific current Hooker communication. Later Niger locality criticism in apparatus is not already established January 17. Hooker year endorsement possibly retrospective; meeting corroborates supplied year.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1982: Additional Gray November 4, 1856 source, all twenty-five blocks including initial eight statistical rows, notes, annotations and bibliography read. Rough 320 European-shared species, 230 not detected inside Arctic circle, minus about twelve alpine/subalpine gives 218; nested latitude thresholds are 155/113/56/20/5, not disjoint bins. Only one of final five a reliable case. Apparatus mentions earlier 321; preserve versions. Answers October 12 letter, later research may extend ranges. Introduced orders supplied while genera requested; list copying not done, reference to buy book not receipt. East Asia climate relation not full causal explanation. Work on mundane genera and corrected lists future. Criticises Hooker conifer ranking; asks Darwin post enclosures. Raw diag/ramme table layout held; Darwin notes undated. Distinctive range facts and conifer rap identify forwarding/knowledge in 1991 by November 18.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1969: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 5 with year supplied, seven blocks and all notes. Requests seeds via George Snow/Nag’s Head/Borough, explicitly a different safer/slower route from water pods; seeds not yet received and identity unclear. Address formatting raw diag/ramme held. Cytisus inquiry results judged too weak; Darwin pleased to disbelieve a rate of change that would be too fast, not general denial of species change. Preserved September 8 outgoing and its later Hooker note are not automatically a full current incoming reply. No identified whole prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1971: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 9 with year supplied, four blocks and full apparatus. Does not remember a recent list; requests named marsh/water pods, having tested sixty or seventy other capsules for flotation. Upcoming London October 15–18 and proposed seed delivery are plans, not already fulfilled. P4 says review read long ago, a retrospective bound distinct from August 5 receipt and August 7 half reading. Missing Hooker inquiry cannot be replaced by Darwin earlier request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1965: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. One-page unsigned Darwin covering note, six blocks, salutation and both notes read. All October 16, 1856 supplied from intended Philosophical Club meeting; hand delivery is likely editorial reconstruction, while posting is admitted possible. Manuscript completed October 13 and read by Hooker November 9, but that does not establish exact delivery day. Requests botanical accuracy, broad/marginal criticism and restraint with unfinished assumptions. Manuscript fragment and back-page notes exist elsewhere but are not transcribed here; covering note is not full chapter or prompt. Retain exact-day review hold despite singleton XML.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Schematic America/Europe northern map, point p, White Mountains and Alps, curved isotherms labelled 40° and 50°, glacial-sea boundary and connecting island/land shapes. Temperature scale is not stated; these are isotherms, not observed latitude contours or a calibrated reconstructed map.

Unlabelled inclined section with a double sloping line, small intermediate rise and hatched cap at upper right, adjacent to humidity/elevation remarks. No numerical dimensions, scale or explicit directional legend; preserve as visual source rather than invent quantified geographic content.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
